text:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated error rate detected on /v1/generate-stream (streaming) — 5xx spike + disconnects in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Alert threshold crossed: 5xx_rate > 3% over 5m. Paging adele (primary on-call).

adele: seeing it, jumping in. quick numbers?

incident-bot: Summary: 5xx (502/504) and upstream timeout errors observed. Many client-side cancellations (RST_STREAM / ECONNRESET). Avg latency increased from 120ms -> 650ms for streaming connections. Root TS: 1718204800.

adele: michael, you around? can you pull logs for the gateway and streaming workers? I'll start customer impact assessment.

michael: I'm here. on it. tailing nginx/gateway logs now: `kubectl -n gateway logs -l app=gateway -f --tail=200`

michael: seeing a pattern — a lot of `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `upstream timed out`. 502s from envoy -> runtime-service. Also seeing `write: broken pipe` on some streaming workers.

sre-jordan: looks like chunked encoding streams are getting closed mid-chunk. Clients report truncated responses and reconnect loops. Could be an app-level worker crash or resource exhaustion. cpu spiking on runtime pods?

infra-eli: checking node metrics. us-west-2 worker nodes at ~78% GPU mem, CPU at 65% but I/O wait is higher on a subset (disk ops). No mass OOMs reported. Kernel logs show repeated `TCP: time wait bucket table overflow` warnings on a single host.

adele: @customer-success-alex please start an impact note for customers with streaming enabled. list likely affected endpoints: streaming chat & streaming generation. Ask CS to watch for complaint spikes.

customer-success-alex: on it. I'll draft an initial message to flagged customers and stand by for mitigation update.

michael: quick mitigation options I see: 1) disable streaming feature flag for affected route (fallback to non-streaming response) 2) increase proxy and upstream timeouts 3) scale up runtime pods + evict high-I/O node 4) roll back last runtime deploy (deploy-bot shows a release 30m ago).

deploy-bot: Recent deploy: runtime-service v1.8.2 by eliza at 1718203000 — health checks passed at deploy.

adele: let's do minimal-customer-impact path: disable streaming for public API in us-west-2 and eu-central first (toggle via config service), then scale up a small pool, and monitor. If that doesn't reduce 5xx, we'll roll back.

michael: disabling streaming flag now on us-west-2. Command: `curl -X POST \"https://config.internal/api/flags\" -d '{\"service\":\"runtime\",\"flag\":\"streaming_enabled\",\"region\":\"us-west-2\",\"value\":false}'`

michael: flag applied. Sending to eu-central now.

michael: flag applied in eu-central. Pushing a soft-config to edge to route new requests as non-streaming.

adele: infra, please scale runtime pods by +3 in both regions (horizontal). use small warm pool so cold starts are minimal.

infra-eli: scaling up now: `kubectl -n runtime scale deployment runtime-service --replicas=10` (was 7). K8s events show 3 new pods scheduling.

michael: also bumping Nginx/Envoy upstream timeouts + proxy_buffer_size and enabling `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_request_buffering off;` to reduce buffering problems for chunked responses while streaming is off — this should help clients not hit partial chunk closes.

adele: good. monitoring dashboards — 1m -> 3m after toggle, 5xx rate in us-west dropped from 4.6% -> 1.2%. eu-central similar drop. latency back to ~160ms for non-streaming requests.

sre-jordan: we should still capture heap/worker crash traces for the pods that had `broken pipe`. Collect `kubectl -n runtime logs POD --previous` and `gcore` if possible. Also check per-connection errors in runtime logs: `ERR: client cancelled` vs `ERR: upstream connect failed`.

michael: grabbing logs from the three highest-err pods. Found repeated exception in worker process: `RuntimeWriteError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe` followed by `Traceback ...` — looks like the worker tried to write to client after client closed connection. But there's also occasional `pyarrow` serialization timeout which correlates with longer requests.

infra-eli: node with TCP timewait overflow — I'm cordoning and draining it to stop new connections hitting it. `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-12` then `kubectl drain` gracefully. Rebalancing connections should help.

customer-success-alex: initial CS message queued: "We're currently investigating intermittent truncated streaming responses and elevated 5xx for streaming endpoints in us-west-2 and eu-central. Temporary mitigation applied: streaming responses temporarily disabled while we stabilize. We'll provide hourly updates."

adele: good. escalation: if error rate doesn't drop below 1% in 15m we're rolling back runtime v1.8.2. michael, are rollbacks quick?

michael: yes, rollback policy available. But let's wait 15m with current mitigations. Also enabling detailed request traces for affected routes (sampler 1%) to capture full end-to-end.

sre-jordan: tracing enabled. adding a regex to capture chunk boundary logs: `grep -E \"chunked|broken pipe|client cancelled|RST_STREAM|upstream prematurely closed\"` across runtime logs and saving to s3: `s3://redwood-incident-logs/1718204823/`.

michael: logs collected. I see a suspicious correlation: requests longer than 8s are much more likely to hit broken pipe. Looks like an upstream keepalive/idle timeout at the TCP proxy was shorter than expected. Need to align timeouts across layers.

infra-eli: adjusted keepalive settings on the host network stack and bumped Envoy idle timeout from 5s -> 15s for the streaming backend. Will monitor for timewait churn.

adele: update: 10m post-mitigation — 5xx rates down to 0.9% in us-west, eu-central 1.0%. Customer complaints only trickling in. Holding.

customer-success-alex: sending update to affected customers: mitigation in place, investigating root cause, ETA next update in 1 hour.

michael: follow-up action items: 1) run load test simulating long-lived streaming clients to reproduce 2) add guard in runtime to stop writes after detecting client disconnect (catch BrokenPipeError and abort early) 3) improve streaming connection lifecycle metrics (per-chunk acks) 4) ensure deploys include streaming stress smoke tests.

adele: jotting down incident timeline and owner assignments. I'll take lead on postmortem. michael -> leads debugging & fixes. infra-eli -> network/timeouts + node remediation. sre-jordan -> logs/trace analysis & retention. cs-alex -> customer comms and impact triage.

michael: note: re-enabling streaming should be a gradual canary with small percentage and warm pool. Also consider a config to disable streaming per-API-key as fallback for enterprise customers.

deploy-bot: Rollback option ready: runtime-service v1.7.9 (previous) verified.

adele: if metrics hold steady for 30m we'll keep streaming disabled and schedule a controlled rollback + patch to worker write handling. If errors reappear, we'll roll back immediately. handoff: my shift ends in 40m — michael, you'll be primary after 08:30UTC.

michael: acknowledged. I'll take handoff and continue monitoring. leaving a short checklist in incident doc.

adele: thanks team. continuing to monitor.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated (streaming disabled, scaled runtime, timeout adjustments). Severity: sev-2 -> watching. Next update scheduled in 30m.

michael: (after 30m) 30m check: error rates stable ~0.7-1.0%. No new deploys. scheduling an on-call playbook update to include streaming canary steps and streaming-specific timeouts.

sre-jordan: collected stack traces & logs saved to `s3://redwood-incident-logs/1718204823/` with tags `streaming-broken-pipe`. Will attach to postmortem.

customer-success-alex: sent second customer update. no escalations so far.

adele: thanks — I'll open the postmortem and link these notes. End of thread for now.
